headline: Google Ads cost per conversion rose from $44.62 to $56.05 (25.6%), 2026-09-27 to 2026-10-10 against 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-24, which is $2,950 of extra cost over 14 days. New broad-match search terms in the generic campaign are the main cause ($1,925, confirmed: the keywords were added on 2026-10-12). A rival pushing up click costs on the competitor campaign ($580, likely) and the same day's budget raise ($140, confirmed) add the rest; $304 is unexplained. The after window ends 4 days ago, past the account's 3-day conversion lag.

conversion_lag.reading: 91.4% of conversions arrive within 3 days of the click, so the after window ends on 2026-10-24, 4 days before 2026-10-28.

windows.not_final: 2026-10-25 to 2026-10-27 are left out: still inside the conversion lag.

the_change.note: Both windows have 14 days, so totals compare the same as daily averages.
the_change.normal_range: Weekly CPA over the eight weeks before 2026-10-11 ran from $42.91 to $46.06. $56.05 is above it: a real rise.
the_change.break_day: 2026-10-17: the first of 3 days in a row with a daily CPA over 125% of the before window's median ($45.00). The account averages 18.6 conversions a day, enough to read a daily CPA.
the_change.dip_in_before_window: none: no run of 3 days with a daily CPA under 80% of the before median
the_change.year_ago: Same weeks a year earlier: CPA $43.50 to $44.45 (2.2%), conversion rate 6.9% to 6.7% (-2.3%). Not the same move, so the season doesn't explain it.

measurement.detail: Both primary actions kept counting: Trial signup 199 to 200, Demo request 61 to 58. No conversion action was added, removed, made primary or secondary, or changed counting type in the change log.

split.how: after cost $14,461 minus 258 conversions at the before CPA of $44.62
split.check: 292 + 2504 + 154 = 2950, the extra cost (unrounded parts add up to the cent).
split.reading: The conversion rate part carries 85% of the extra cost, almost all of it in the generic campaign ($2,400). Click cost is $292: the competitor campaign's CPC rose $4.00 to $5.00 ($580), while the generic campaign's fell (-$290). Mix is $154, under 10% of the extra cost.

device_lens.check: the pieces add up to the campaign's own $2,110
device_lens.reading: Conversion rate fell on desktop (-28.6%) and mobile (-25.8%) alike, and the shift between devices is $9: not a device problem.

competitor_device_lens.check: the pieces add up to the campaign's own $600
competitor_device_lens.reading: CPC rose on desktop ($4.22 to $5.20) and mobile ($3.67 to $4.70) alike, and the shift between devices is -$1: the click cost rose inside each device, not from a move between them.

search_terms.rows_cover: 91.0% of the campaign's cost before and 92.4% after

new_terms.search_term: how to make an appointment calendar

search_terms.held_terms_test: The 7 terms with clicks in both windows converted at 4.3% before and 4.2% after (-1.4%), within 10%: the drop came from the new traffic, so landing page, device and season are ruled out for this campaign.

causes.evidence: Measurement passed: both primary actions kept counting at the same level, and no conversion action changed.
The generic campaign's daily budget went from $450 to $650 on 2026-10-12. Its share of conversions rose from 30.8% to 32.6%, at a before CPA of $75.00 against the account's $44.62.
The shift between devices is $9 in the generic campaign and -$1 in the competitor campaign, where CPC rose on both devices; all clicks in both are on Search.
No bid strategy or target change in the change log, and no campaign is learning now.

Competitor campaign CPC $4.00 to $5.00 with no edit on it. Impression share lost to rank 22% to 35%, top impression share 48% to 39%. In the pasted auction insights, competitor-b.example overlap rate rose 38% to 61% and outranking share 31% to 47%. Likely, not confirmed: nothing dates the rival's move.
Impression-weighted Quality Score moved 6.8 to 6.6 on the generic campaign and 5.3 to 5.4 on the competitor campaign, under the 0.5 bar.

6 terms that never showed before took $2,300 and 880 clicks for 5 conversions (0.6% against the campaign's 4.0% before). They start after 2 broad-match keywords were added to the generic campaign on 2026-10-12, the day after the after window opens. The terms that ran in both windows held their rate (-1.4%).
Held-terms test passed, and the main landing page /features/online-booking/ answers 200 with no redirect.
Conversion rate fell on both devices by a similar amount, and the held terms held.
A year earlier the conversion rate moved -2.3% over the same weeks, against -17.2% now.

unexplained.reading: $2,950 extra cost minus $2,645 claimed by confirmed and likely causes (each figure is rounded on its own, so they can differ by $1). Where it sits: the generic campaign's own dollars beyond the new terms $185; the competitor campaign's conversion rate $20; mix in the other campaigns $14; Brand (all parts) $25; Industry: Salons (all parts) $60.

causes_not_applicable: New campaign and budget limits: no campaign was added or newly limited in the windows. Order value: this is a CPA question with no conversion value. The change log's only other edit, one headline reworded on Industry: Salons on 2026-10-06, sits in a campaign whose own dollars are $60, left in the unexplained.

what_to_do.action: In the generic campaign, add the 6 new terms as negatives (the job, iPhone, Excel and free-app searches first), or pause the 2 broad keywords added on 2026-10-12 and go back to phrase match.
Keep the generic budget at $450 a day until its CPA is back near $75.00, then raise it in steps.
On the competitor campaign, hold the target CPA. Check competitor-b.example's ads in the auction for a new offer before you raise bids.

recheck: If the fixes go in on 2026-10-29, recheck on 2026-11-15: 14 days after the fix plus the 3-day lag.
could_not_check: Change history for 2026-09-27 to 2026-09-28: change_event only reaches back 30 days. The Change history export would cover those days.
Auction insights for the generic campaign: only the competitor campaign's table was pasted.
